Data is only useful if it actually reflects reality.  Preferring data over actual common sense is foolish.

You can collect data that supports a point, or collect data that refutes a point, and in either case just not be collecting other data which might throw off the results you're trying to "prove".  Studies and statistics are extremely easy to bias.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
When your expectations do not match your results, then either your expectations are wrong, or your model is.  Assuming that either one is correct is foolish.  Find why there is a descrepancy (or at least why there might be a descrepancy), and make your decision based on that.

 

For example:  dclietz expected AZ to improve in H=5 games more than he did because he benfits from pumping.  One possible explaination is that there are few enough pumping heroes that 5H doesn't significantly improve AZ's chances of being pumped.  So now you can do math to investigate whether this is likely, or if the source of the discrepancy is elsewhere.

posts.cooked:
But everything falls within the mean. If it doesn't it's an indication that something has changed.

Jimmy, a slot machine is, in and of itself, an X factor in the equation. As for using a shooting range for an analogy, the person shooting should be improving if they do it often enough, and the gun is not in the same exact position with each shot. Statistics tries to minimize variables, or at least track them.
